body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\). If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every permitted directed lag and bidirected offset. The ancestors of \(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\}\) in \(G^\star\) lie in \(V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\), contain at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices, and one ordinary ID call on this ancestral ADMG is sound and complete for uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with every returned probability evaluated on the common product alphabet.
body.justification: The proposition supplies a nontrivial solved subclass and a required reduction test for the general transducer.
body.gap: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui use a densest candidate full-time graph to validate adjustment under causal sufficiency, and Jahn--Karnik--Schulman analyze one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph. This reduction instead uses one saturated ancestral ADMG to decide general fixing-based identification uniformly over unknown lag refinements and supplies exact-summary stationary negative witnesses.
body.consumer: Acyclic EasyRCA summaries can be screened immediately with an ordinary finite ID implementation.
